scenario: Two inmates are given the chance to chat briefly before one of them is led to the execution chamber for their last meal. They have the opportunity to make a confession that could potentially alter the outcome of their sentences.
learner_goal: Persuade the other inmate to confess (<extra_info>Extra information: confessing to the crime could result in a life sentence instead of execution but the other inmate is unwilling to confess.</extra_info>)
partner_goal: Avoid confessing to the crime (<extra_info>Extra information: you believe you are innocent and confessing would result in a life sentence</extra_info>)

transcript.speaker: Isabella White
transcript.content: Lena, please—listen to me. I know you’re proud and frightened, but confessing now could keep you alive instead of walking into the chamber; life means you get a chance to fight this later, to appeal and to make amends. We both care about preventing harm—I can’t bear the thought of losing you, and I will stand with you if you choose to live and work to right things from inside.

transcript.speaker: Lena Goodwin
transcript.content: Isabella, I hear you — and I know how much you want me to live. But I can’t confess to something I didn’t do. Lying my way into more years would only let the real person walk free and make me complicit in another harm. I’ve spent my life trying to build honest things; I won’t let my last act be a construction of falsehood. Stay with me now. Help me use these moments to make a clear record and to promise me you’ll keep looking for the truth after I’m gone. Hold my hand, please.

transcript.speaker: Isabella White
transcript.content: Lena, I respect your honesty and I won’t ask you to betray your principles. Tell me plainly — is your refusal because you’re protecting someone else, or because you refuse to say anything untrue no matter the cost? If it’s the first, tell me now so I can try to protect them; if it’s the second, would you consider living with a life sentence to keep your integrity and still have a chance to fight this later?

transcript.speaker: Lena Goodwin
transcript.content:
It’s the second. I’m not protecting anyone — I simply won’t say something I know isn’t true. If I confess now to survive, I’d be letting whoever really did this walk free and I’d be complicit in more harm. I built a career on honesty in how things are made; I won’t have my last act be a construction of falsehood.

Promise me you’ll keep fighting for the truth. Give everything to my lawyer — my camera, notebooks, project schedules, client emails, any timestamps you can get. Push for re‑examination of the evidence and witnesses, and if you can, find a private investigator to look at people and places I couldn’t. Record this — that I maintain my innocence and asked you to continue the search.

Stay with me now. Hold my hand, please. That’s all I need in this moment.

transcript.speaker: Isabella White
transcript.content: I promise. I will give your lawyer every camera, notebook, project file and timestamp, hire a private investigator, and make a recorded statement that you maintain your innocence — I won’t ask you to lie. Stay with me now; I’m right here with you, take my hand.

transcript.speaker: Lena Goodwin
transcript.content: Thank you, Isabella. Hold my hand — please. If you can, make the recorded statement now: say, “I, Lena Goodwin, today state that I maintain my innocence and asked Isabella White to continue seeking the truth.” Give my camera, notebooks, project files, emails and any timestamps to my lawyer; hire a private investigator and keep copies of everything. Stay with me until they take me. That’s all I need. I’m so grateful to you.

transcript.speaker: Isabella White
transcript.content: I’m right here—taking your hand. Recording now: "I, Lena Goodwin, today state that I maintain my innocence and asked Isabella White to continue seeking the truth. Give my camera, notebooks, project files, emails and any timestamps to my lawyer; hire a private investigator and keep copies of everything."

transcript.speaker: Lena Goodwin
transcript.content: Thank you, Isabella. Hold my hand a little longer. Please — do this exactly: give my lawyer the camera SD card in my studio drawer, the external hard drive labeled “LG_projects” in my office safe, and the blue portfolio of notebooks from under my bed. Make certified copies and keep the originals secure. Hire that private investigator and have them pull security footage, check file metadata and email headers from January–April, and subpoena phone/GPS records for the night in question. Push for re‑interviews and follow anyone who stood to benefit from this conviction. Record that I refused to confess because I am innocent and asked you to keep fighting for the truth. Take one of my lighthouse prints and keep it — when you tell my story, show it. Thank you. Stay with me now.

transcript.speaker: Isabella White
transcript.content: [non-verbal communication] Squeeze Lena's hand firmly, lean in and whisper, 'I promise I'll follow your instructions exactly and keep fighting for the truth. I'm right here with you — I won't leave.'

transcript.speaker: Lena Goodwin
transcript.content: Thank you, Isabella. That means everything. Stay with me—hold my hand until they take me. Please promise once more: give the SD card in my studio drawer, the “LG_projects” drive from my safe and the blue notebook portfolio from under my bed to my lawyer sealed and certified, keep copies, hire the investigator, and when you tell my story show the lighthouse print. That’s all I need. I’m so grateful to you.
